# fjordrun_template_deployment (Resource)

Deploys a template (`fjordrun_templates` lists them) into a project: creates its services, in every environment, with their generated secrets and volumes, and deploys them to `environment_id`. To run them in another environment too, add a `fjordrun_deployment` for that environment.

This resource owns the set of services, not their settings. Change those with `fjordrun_service_environment`, and add variables with `fjordrun_service_variables` and `exclusive = false`, which keeps the generated secrets.

**Destroy.** With `on_destroy = "delete"` (the default) destroying this resource **deletes the template's services in all environments, including their volumes and data**. With `on_destroy = "keep"` they stay, unmanaged. For a database, also set `lifecycle { prevent_destroy = true }`.

**Drift.** A service deleted outside Terraform disappears from `services` with a warning; the others are kept. This resource is replaced only if all are gone. Use `terraform apply -replace` to start over.

**Import.** `project_id/environment_id/template` adopts every service of that template in the project.

## Example Usage

```terraform
variable "team_id" {
  type = string
}

resource "fjordrun_project" "shop" {
  team_id = var.team_id
  name    = "shop"
}

resource "fjordrun_template_deployment" "postgres" {
  project_id     = fjordrun_project.shop.id
  environment_id = fjordrun_project.shop.default_environment_id
  template       = "postgres"
  wait           = true

  lifecycle {
    # destroying this resource deletes the database and its data
    prevent_destroy = true
  }
}

output "postgres_service_id" {
  value = fjordrun_template_deployment.postgres.service_ids["Postgres"]
}

data "fjordrun_service_access" "postgres" {
  service_id     = fjordrun_template_deployment.postgres.service_ids["Postgres"]
  environment_id = fjordrun_project.shop.default_environment_id
}

output "connection_url" {
  value     = data.fjordrun_service_access.postgres.values["Connection URL"]
  sensitive = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `environment_id` (String) The environment to deploy to.
- `project_id` (String) Project ID.
- `template` (String) Template code, such as `postgres`.

### Optional

- `on_destroy` (String) `delete` (default) deletes the services and their volumes on destroy; `keep` leaves them.
- `timeouts` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--timeouts))
- `wait` (Boolean) Wait until every service's first deployment finishes, up to the `create` timeout (default 30 minutes), and fail the apply unless they succeed.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) `project_id/environment_id/template`.
- `service_ids` (Map of String) Service IDs by name, for example `fjordrun_template_deployment.db.service_ids["Postgres"]`.
- `services` (Attributes List) The services the template created. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--services))

<a id="nestedatt--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).


<a id="nestedatt--services"></a>
### Nested Schema for `services`

Read-Only:

- `id` (String) Service ID.
- `image` (String) Container image.
- `kind` (String) Service kind.
- `name` (String) Service name.
- `private_hostname` (String) Hostname within the environment.
- `slug` (String) Service slug.
- `status` (String) Status in `environment_id`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# project_id/environment_id/template: adopts every service of that template in the project
terraform import fjordrun_template_deployment.postgres 55555555-5555-5555-5555-555555555555/66666666-6666-6666-6666-666666666666/postgres
```
